about: Historical context for A Tale of Two Cities: the real events of the French Revolution around the fictional story.

entries.modern: The Bastille fortress-prison in Paris was stormed on 14 July 1789; it then held only seven prisoners. The day is France's national holiday.
sources: Simon Schama, Citizens: A Chronicle of the French Revolution (1989)
William Doyle, The Oxford History of the French Revolution (2nd ed. 2002)
entries.relationship: Real event; Doctor Manette's cell, One Hundred and Five, North Tower, and the Defarges' part in the attack are fiction.

entries.topic: The prison of La Force and the September Massacres
match: You are consigned, Evrémonde, to the prison of La Force
entries.modern: La Force was a real Paris prison; in the September Massacres (2–6 September 1792) crowds killed about 1,100–1,400 prisoners in Paris, including over 160 at La Force.
sources: William Doyle, The Oxford History of the French Revolution (2nd ed. 2002)
Frédéric Bluche, Septembre 1792: logiques d'un massacre (1986)
entries.relationship: Real place and events; Darnay's imprisonment there is fiction.

match: the sharp female called La Guillotine
entries.modern: The guillotine was adopted in 1792; during the Terror (September 1793 – July 1794) about 17,000 people were officially executed in France, some 2,600 of them in Paris.
sources: Donald Greer, The Incidence of the Terror during the French Revolution (1935)
entries.relationship: Real; Sydney Carton's death on the scaffold is fiction.
